platforms.name: Uber Eats
platforms.summary: Public store pages publish the whole menu with USD prices and the branch's street address as schema.org data, so each price is tied to one US branch.
evidence: Prices read from real US store pages in every live run since 37708779121 (up to 335 menu items per page); 40 branches in the 00:01 UTC run on 9 Oct.
Store links come from robots.txt-declared sitemaps and brand pages. Non-US country sections are skipped without a request.
A few store pages answered with a challenge. Those are counted as blocked and not worked around.
Uber's US terms (read from uber.com on 2026-10-18) bar scripts that unduly burden or hinder the service; unlike Uber's terms for India, they do not mention scraping.

platforms.name: DoorDash
platforms.summary: Branch discovery works, but store pages answer datacenter requests with a Cloudflare challenge, so no current DoorDash branch price could be read from a server. Type the prices you see in the DoorDash app instead (below).
evidence: 99 of 99 store-page requests across 20 live runs returned 403 “Just a moment…”.
131 per-state/province store sitemaps are readable (California alone lists 106,409 store URLs).
/business/…/menu pages show prices DoorDash labels “estimated based on your predicted location”, so they are not used as branch prices.

15 archived copies of real store pages per probe run (Wayback Machine; the latest, 2026-10-15, holds captures from Jul 2024 to Oct 2026) show the layout: Restaurant + Menu JSON-LD on 11 (a bare Menu on 3, nothing on 1 from 2024), prices like “$8.53” or “$13.59+” (a starting price), no currency field and no ZIP. The reader handles it: 8 US stores read with USD prices, 3 Canadian excluded. Archived prices are never used.
The capture bookmarklet is switched off on DoorDash pages: DoorDash's terms forbid copying its site with scripts, even ones you run yourself.

platforms.name: Grubhub
platforms.summary: Grubhub's restaurant pages are drawn by JavaScript and publish no prices. Two Grubhub-owned menu sites publish the same restaurants' menus with prices and link back to each Grubhub listing, so a menu is used only when it links to the same Grubhub restaurant ID.
evidence: MenuPages: Lou Malnati's, 6456 S Cicero Ave, Chicago (Grubhub ID 434510), 168 priced listings of 170 from its Menu JSON-LD in the newest run. Its restaurant sitemap lists 28,033 pages.

AllMenus: Lou Malnati's, 85 S Buffalo Grove Rd (ID 517712, not on MenuPages), 165 priced listings in the newest run. Prices are read from the page HTML only because its 216 item names match the page's own JSON-LD names.
A menu is used only from a page that links to exactly that one Grubhub restaurant; a blocked or incomplete lookup is reported as such.
Published menu prices can lag the live Grubhub menu (AllMenus says its menus may not be current) and leave out option charges.
Grubhub's terms limit both sites to personal, non-commercial use and forbid automated access; operators can switch the lookups off (FPC_DISABLE_GRUBHUB_MIRRORS=1).

alternatives.intro: 24 ways to get this data were researched in October 2026, each claim was re-checked by an independent search, and a final pass looked for anything missed (it added five). Prices for arbitrary US branches come only from public pages today: every official API is limited to partners. “Not usable” means the method breaks this app's rules (no bypassing bot checks, no private APIs) or the provider's terms.

methods.name: Uber Eats public store pages (schema.org JSON-LD)
methods.how: Each store page publishes its menu, USD prices and street address as structured data.
methods.access: None: public pages, robots.txt allows them.
methods.fit_note: Uber's US terms bar scripts that unduly burden the service; runs are spaced 3 s apart, and pages that answer with a challenge are reported, not bypassed.

methods.name: MenuPages (Grubhub-owned)
methods.how: Grubhub menus as JSON-LD with USD prices; each page links to its Grubhub listing.
methods.access: None: public pages, robots.txt allows them.
methods.fit_note: Covers a subset of Grubhub (28,033 pages). Terms: personal, non-commercial use only.

methods.name: AllMenus (Grubhub-owned)
methods.how: Menu prices in the page HTML, item names in JSON-LD, a link to the Grubhub listing.
methods.access: None: public pages, robots.txt allows them.
methods.fit_note: Used only when HTML and JSON-LD names agree. Same Grubhub terms as MenuPages.

methods.name: Uber Eats brand-city pages
methods.how: Lists a chain's Uber Eats stores in a city with links to each store page.
methods.branch_prices: No (sample prices are not tied to a branch)
methods.fit_note: Useful for finding store pages; prices still come from each store page.

methods.name: Capture bookmarklet in your own browser
methods.how: Reads the schema.org menu data of the Uber Eats store page you are viewing and gives you JSON to import. On DoorDash pages it stops and points to typed entry.
methods.access: You run it on pages you open.
methods.branch_prices: Yes for fixed Uber Eats prices; “$0.00” and “+” prices are kept as not published
methods.fit_note: Switched off on DoorDash, whose terms ban copying its site with scripts, even manually run ones. Uber's US terms bar scripts that unduly burden the service, so on Uber Eats it is your call.

methods.name: Prices you saw, typed in
methods.how: You open the store in the DoorDash or Uber Eats app or site as you normally would and type the prices it shows, with the store link for the store ID.
methods.access: Your app or browser; no scraping.
methods.branch_prices: Yes, for your branch, order mode and account
methods.fit_note: The scraping-free way to include DoorDash. Entries are validated like any import and labelled Imported.

methods.name: Your order receipts (paste or upload)
methods.how: Item lines and prices from your own receipts.
methods.branch_prices: No: your past orders, no store ID
methods.fit_note: Good for your Grubhub side of the comparison; never current prices for other stores.

methods.name: Personal data downloads (Uber Privacy Center, DoorDash archive)
methods.how: Your own past orders with item prices, requested from each platform.
methods.branch_prices: No: no store address or URL
methods.fit_note: Low risk, but only your own past orders.

methods.name: Screenshots of the app's menu or cart (OCR, you confirm)
methods.how: You share the store link and a screenshot from the mobile app; text is read on your device and you confirm it.
methods.branch_prices: Yes, for the branch, address and mode you chose
methods.fit_note: OCR was not built; typing the prices in covers the same need, and you confirm every value either way.

methods.name: Grubhub page captured in your own browser
methods.how: A bookmarklet would read the Grubhub page after its own scripts have drawn it.
methods.fit_note: This project never saw the rendered Grubhub markup, so no selectors were written; Grubhub's terms forbid scraping.

methods.name: DoorDash Marketplace API
methods.how: Partner API returning a store's menu with delivery and pickup prices.
methods.access: Approved POS/middleware partners under a signed agreement.
methods.branch_prices: Only the partner's own connected stores
methods.fit_note: Cannot read arbitrary DoorDash stores; not open to a comparison app.

methods.name: Uber Eats Marketplace APIs
methods.how: Partner menu and store APIs with full per-store menus.
methods.access: NDA, API licence and a business agreement with Uber.
methods.branch_prices: Only stores that activated your app
methods.fit_note: Uber has used its API terms against price comparison before.

methods.name: Grubhub partner / POS APIs
methods.how: Menu ingestion and retrieval for integrated merchants.
methods.fit_note: Grubhub's consumer api-gtm host is a private backend and off-limits.

methods.name: Menu middleware (Deliverect, Otter, Checkmate, Olo)
methods.how: Per-channel menu prices that merchants push to each platform.
methods.access: Partner agreement plus each restaurant's consent.
methods.fit_note: Shows the merchant's intended price, which the platform can override.

methods.name: MealMe API
methods.how: Licensed B2B menu and ordering API with its own store IDs.
methods.access: API key request and a signed licence.
methods.branch_prices: Yes, but not the DoorDash or Uber Eats listing
methods.fit_note: Returns no DoorDash/Uber Eats price, store ID or URL, so it cannot verify platform prices.

methods.name: E-receipt panel data (Edison Trends)
methods.how: Consented e-receipt panel covering delivery orders.
methods.fit_note: Analytics only, not current branch prices.

methods.name: DoorDash CLI (dd-cli)
methods.how: Official command-line tool for a logged-in consumer.
methods.fit_note: Its access terms forbid price comparison, aggregation and storing results.

methods.name: Unblocking scraping APIs (Zyte, ScraperAPI, Oxylabs, Bright Data …)
methods.how: Proxies that fetch pages through residential IPs.
methods.fit_note: They get past DoorDash's Cloudflare by spoofing fingerprints and solving CAPTCHAs, which this app never does.

methods.name: Apify store actors for Uber Eats and Grubhub
methods.how: Community scrapers run on demand.
methods.fit_note: They rely on residential proxies or Grubhub's private api-gtm endpoints.

methods.name: DoorDash /business/…/menu pages
methods.how: Chain-level menu with prices.
methods.fit_note: “Prices are estimated based on your predicted location.” Used for store discovery only.

methods.name: DoorDash Storefront pages (order.online)
methods.how: Restaurants' first-party ordering pages.
methods.branch_prices: First-party base price, not the DoorDash delivery price
methods.fit_note: Different prices from Marketplace, and the Storefront terms ban scraping.

methods.name: Yelp menu pages
methods.how: Menu pages on Yelp.
methods.access: Paid Places API has only a menu link.
methods.fit_note: DoorDash now powers most Yelp ordering, and Yelp's terms forbid scraping.

methods.name: Archives and old datasets (Wayback, Common Crawl, Kaggle)
methods.how: Captured copies of public pages, months to years old.
methods.fit_note: Never used as prices. Used as evidence of page structure: 15 archived DoorDash store pages per probe run verified the DoorDash reader (11 of them carry a Restaurant block) (existing captures only; Common Crawl's index robots.txt disallows the queries, which is honoured). Wayback is for research, non-commercial use; the Kaggle Uber Eats dump has no store ID, URL or timestamp and is for educational use.

methods.name: Uber Consumer Delivery APIs
methods.how: Official APIs for consumer apps: find merchants, browse menus and items, carts, with Uber account linking.
methods.fit_note: The one official Uber surface that reaches arbitrary stores; response fields were not confirmed.

methods.name: Distribution partnerships (Grubhub and Uber Eats in ChatGPT, Alexa+, Eater …)
methods.how: Platforms already send live listings and menu items to selected outside apps.
methods.access: A bilateral business deal; no public program.
methods.fit_note: The legitimate route to live Grubhub menus at scale.

methods.name: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) food ordering
methods.how: An open agentic-commerce protocol with a food working group that includes DoorDash and Uber Eats.
methods.access: Waitlist; the food menu spec is not published yet.
methods.fit_note: Worth watching: it may become a documented route to DoorDash and Uber Eats menus without a bilateral contract.
